AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: supporting the health and wellbeing of healthcare employees is a national priority in the UK.

AbstractText.Label: AIMS
AbstractText.content: to design, deliver and evaluate an educational package to promote health and wellbeing for nurses and midwives.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: an online training package was developed and administered in two ways: online (HAWN-online) or in a face-to-face workshop (HAWN-contact). A mixed methods evaluation was used to assess usability and acceptability of HAWN training.

AbstractText.Label: FINDINGS
AbstractText.content: 316 nurses, midwives and students completed the online training package and 16 participants attended the workshop. HAWN-online significantly increased knowledge in core areas of workplace health and wellbeing. Nurses and midwives valued online and face-to-face delivery but found there were barriers to attendance at workshops. Participants advocated that training in workplace health should be mandatory for all frontline staff.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSIONS
AbstractText.content: employers should take steps to promote staff wellbeing through HAWN training, and address barriers to accessing workplace health training or supportive services.
